evidence: The task is written for this product throughout. instruction.md:1-13 describes HireOps's own two-sided problem: a shared per-job pipeline board plus a recruiter-candidate conversation on each application, with several people using it at once. hireops_rules.md sections 3-7 author product-specific mechanics: a six-stage board with hand-arranged in-stage order (s3 'Order inside a stage'), per-job interview places 1-50, hiring-manager rights limited to late stages, version-based 409 refusals that name the colleague, multi-card moves that arrive in board order, own-last-move undo blocked by later touches, 30-message paged threads that keep the reader's place, per-person unread and seen rules (the observer never counts), drafts kept per user and conversation across sign-out, and a candidate-wording table. Every criterion uses the hro_ prefix and names HireOps entities and seeded people (Rafael, Mei Lin, Noor Haddad's 120-message Platform Engineer thread, Lena's 1 unread; functional/judge.toml lines 26-419). Polish and visual rows are product-specific too (hro_pol_live_board, hro_pol_earlier_place, hro_vis_color 'stage markers and the rejected stage'), not template copies. A grep of the frozen task for sibling product names (Pellmoor, Colderwater, BazaarBridge, Ridgeline, TorqueBay, Docketlight, Boardloom, Northstar, vacancy, CHANGE_ME) found nothing. A grep for leftovers from the earlier HireOps offer/approval design (rescind, approval, hro_dual, compensation, change-set) also found nothing outside unrelated UI 'preview' text and the frozen Dockerfile's approval_policy. Sibling comparison: the closest sibling is projects/pellmoor-job-pipeline, which is also a hiring pipeline. The two share only generic pipeline rules: no stage skipping, one email per vacancy, a stale-write 409 and an all-or-nothing batch. Their flows and criteria differ. Pellmoor centres on interview panels, 1-5 scores, assessment versioning and invalidation, offer+hired opening capacity, a reviewed batch-offer preview with durable actor-scoped retry receipts, and a d3 funnel built from stage history. Its criterion ids include exact_derived_funnel, panel_change_invalidates_entire_assessment and successful_retry_replays_one_result, and it uses the retired reward.toml layout. HireOps has no panels, scores, funnel or receipts. It is about board ordering, undo, live sync that preserves focus, scroll and drafts, and a messaging half: paging, unread, seen, drafts and the candidate portal. About half the functional weight has no counterpart in Pellmoor. Threadline-chat shares the unread concept but is a Slack-style channel product with no pipeline. So this is not a nouns-swapped clone: neither the flows nor the criteria match. Domain plan: task.toml:15 arena_slice='recruiting-hiring-operations' is unique among the 37 project task.toml files. provenance (task.toml:14) says the task was adapted from a supplied HireOps task, so the domain was assigned. No separate suite domain-plan file exists in the workspace; NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md:203 asks only for distinct domain behaviour, which this meets. Weak/alternative test for this row: a renamed Pellmoor (vacancies to jobs, panels kept) would fail almost every hro_ conversation, undo, order and live row, so the rubric itself shows the difference; a different but conforming recruiting desk would not be penalised by this row. Lessons file check: the portal flags it lists (rows 1, 25, 28, 32, 35) do not bear on row 53. The drift lesson (17-18) was checked by grepping for residue of the earlier HireOps design, and none was found. No runtime evidence is needed for this row, so none is missing.
notes: Non-blocking observations, not defects: (1) The suite now holds two recruiting-domain tasks (HireOps and Pellmoor). They are mechanically distinct, but if a client-side domain plan caps one task per domain, the owner should confirm that HireOps's assigned 'supplied HireOps task' provenance covers it. (2) arena_slice omits the stack prefix that most siblings use (e.g. full-stack-node-express-sqlite-...). This is cosmetic and is not graded by this row.
